title.narrative: Bridging the gap in GBV coordination and local leadership amidst funding crises.

description.narrative: The humanitarian landscape in South Sudan is currently facing an unprecedented funding crisis that has severely destabilized the Gender-Based Violence (GBV) coordination mechanism at both national and state levels. As the primary Women-Led Organization (WLO) co-chairing the National GBV Area of Responsibility (AoR), Women for Change (WFC) has observed a dangerous erosion of the protective environment for women and girls. The reduction in funding has not merely limited activities; it has dismantled the essential infrastructure required to convene partners, harmonize life-saving approaches, and ensure accountability to survivors. According to recent GBV AoR surveys, an estimated USD 12 million has been slashed from prevention and response efforts, leading to the layoff of approximately 503 specialized staff, including caseworkers, healthcare providers, and counselors. This drain of human capital has crippled the ability to collect, analyze, and disseminate data on GBV trends, effectively silencing the evidence base required for advocacy. Furthermore, the closure of at least 37 Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) has removed the only safe havens available for thousands of women, increasing their vulnerability to sexual exploitation and abuse. Without robust coordination, referral pathways have become fragmented, leaving survivors to navigate a broken system without timely or quality support, thereby compromising the "Survivor-Centered Approach" that is the gold standard of our work.
